picked.body: 빈패스트의 전기차 VF8. 베트남이 전동화 차량 보급률 기준 세계 10대 시장에 이름을 올렸다. 이는 지난 수년에 걸친 정부 주도의 친환경 모빌리티 전환이 가속화된 데 따른 영향으로 풀이된다. 국제에너지기구(IEA)는 최근 이러한 내용을 담은 세계 전동화 차량 도입 현황에 대한 보고서를 발표했다. 해당 보고서는 전 세계 신차 판매량 대비 플러그인하이브리드(PHEV)와 순수전기차(BEV) 등을 포함한 전동화 차량 비중을 기준으로, 전동화 차량 시장 점유율 상위 10개국을 평가했다. 베트남을 포함한 상위 10개국 대부분은 전동화 차량 도입이 가속화되고 있으며, 신차 판매 대수 대비 전동화 차량 비중은 2020년 10% 수준에서 작년 기준 30% 이상, 일부는 70% 가까이 확대되는 모습을 보였다. IEA와 베트남자동차제조업협회(VAMA), 빈패스트(VinFast) 자료를 종합하면 베트남은 작년 기준 전동화 차량 비중에서 상위 10개국 중 8위에 올랐다. 그중에서도 베트남과 우루과이의 사례는 특히 이례적인데, 2020년에는 전기차가 거의 없었지만, 작년 비중이 약 30%까지 늘었기 때문이다. 빈패스트는 지난해 전체 신차 판매량 60만4,000여 대 가운데 전기차로만 17만5,000여 대를 기록했다. 베트남 내 하이브리드 차량은 주로 비야디(BYD)와 기아, 메르세데스, 볼보 등이 판매하고 있지만, 판매량은 유의미한 비중을 차지하지 않고 있다. 이 때문에 베트남 내 전동화 차량 판매량은 사실상 빈패스트 판매량으로 대표되고 있으며, 이를 기준으로 한 전기차 비중은 전체의 약 29%에 이른 것으로 추정된다. IEA에 따르면 지난해 베트남의 전동화 차량 판매 비중은 세계 평균(25%)보다 높다. 또한 호주(15%), 한국(11%), 미국(10%) 등 여러 주요 시장보다도 훨씬 높은 수준이다. 베트남의 전동화 차량 보급률은 동남아에서도 1위를 달리고 있다. 베트남에 이어 태국은 전동화 차량 비중 25%로 세계 11위에 올랐다. 7월 기준 베트남 내 순수전기차 판매 대수는 누적 13만7,773대로 전년 동기 대비 74% 증가해 전체 신차 판매량의 약 35.5%를 차지했다. 지난 2년간 순수전기차는 베트남 자동차 시장의 핵심 성장 동력으로 그 입지를 강화하고 있다. 중국산 브랜드가 큰 영향력을 행사하며 전기차 시장을 주도하는 다른 역내국과 달리, 베트남은 자국 브랜드 빈패스트의 독주 체제를 보이고 있다. 경쟁사들의 판매량이 아직 미미한 수준이라, 이 회사의 판매량이 곧 베트남 전기차 전체 판매량이라고 봐도 무방한 상황이다. IEA는 베트남의 전동화차량 전체 비중이 2035년까지 판매량의 80%에 이를 수 있으며, 이는 동남아시아 전체에서 가장 높은 수준이 될 것으로 전망했다. 전동화차량 판매를 견인하는 요인으로는 차량 가격의 접근성 향상과 특별소비세·등록세 면제·감면 같은 정부의 장려 정책이 꼽힌다. 한편, IEA는 베트남의 전동화 차량 비중이 2035년까지 전체 신차 판매량의 80%에 이를 수 있으며, 이를 통해 동남아에서 전동화 차량 도입이 가장 빠른 국가가 될 것으로 전망했다. 베트남 내 전동화 차량 판매를 주도하는 요인으로는 경쟁력있는 차량 가격과 정부의 특별소비세 및 등록세 감면 등의 정책이 꼽힌다.

picked.t: 베트남, 예금금리 상승세 지속…6개월물 최고 연 9.2% 도달
picked.body: 기사 이해를 돕기위해 AI를 활용해 제작한 이미지입니다. 올 들어 베트남 은행권의 수신 경쟁이 지속되고 있는 가운데, 일부 은행에서는 6개월 만기 상품의 금리가 최고 연 9.2%까지 치솟은 것으로 나타났다. 하노이 서호(Tay Ho) 지역에 거주 중인 한 지역민 A씨는 현지 매체 뚜오이쩨(Tuoitre)에 최근 VP은행(VPBank)에 예치했던 10억 동(3.8만여 달러) 규모의 정기예금을 해지했다고 밝혔다. 해당 계좌는 연 6.4% 금리의 6개월 만기 상품으로, 만기 자금이 자동으로 재예치되고 있었다. VP은행은 A씨의 만기 시점, 온라인 기준 6개월 만기 상품에 연 8.8% 금리를 제시했다. 이는 기존과 비교해 2.4%포인트 높은 수준으로, 6개월 및 12개월 만기 상품에 모두 이 같은 금리를 제시한 것으로 전해졌다. 또 다른 하노이 지역민 B씨에 따르면, 사이공하노이은행(SHB)도 10억 동 예치 고객에게 더 높은 금리를 제시하고 있다. 지난달 28일 기준 6개월 만기 상품의 금리는 연 9.2%로, 2주 전보다 0.2%포인트 올랐다. 업계에서는 지금과 같이 사업 여건이 어려운 상황에서 연 9% 안팎의 예금금리는 매력적인 수준이라는 반응이 나온다. 현재로선 예금이 높은 수익성을 보장하면서도 안전한 자산 운용 수단이라는 평가다. 반면 국영은행권 금리는 민간은행에 비해서는 훨씬 낮은 수준이다. 아그리은행(Agribank) 홈페이지에 게시된 공시금리표에 따르면 해당 은행의 창구 최고금리는 연 6%로, 24~36개월 만기 상품에 적용된다. 이 외 만기별 예금금리는 1개월 연 2.6%, 3개월 연 2.9%, 6~11개월 연 4%, 12개월 연 5.9% 수준이다. 비엣콤은행(Vietcombank)은 온라인 가입 기준 6개월·9개월물 예금금리가 연 3.5%다. 이 은행의 최고금리는 연 6%로, 24개월물에 적용된다. 예금금리가 지속적인 상승세를 보이고 있는 가운데, 최근 베트남 은행권은 다양한 저금리 대출 프로그램을 잇따라 내놓고 있다. 앞서 베트남 4대 국영상업은행을 비롯한 총 12개 은행은 지난달 말 중소기업의 자금난 해소를 지원하기 위해 총액 408조 동(156억1,950만여 달러) 규모 저금리 신용 프로그램을 발표했다. 은행권의 이 같은 움직임은 레 민 흥(Le Minh Hung) 총리와 베트남중앙은행(SBV)이 경제 성장을 뒷받침하기 위해 실질 대출금리 인하를 지시하고 나선 이후 나온 조치로 많은 주목을 받고 있다.

picked.t: Vietnam nominates 5 candidates for World's Best Tourism Village
picked.body: The National Tourism Administration announced that five destinations have been put forward for UN Tourism’s annual "Best Tourism Villages" award. They are Lo (Dak Lak Province), Cat Cat Community Tourism Village (Lao Cai Province), Bay Mau Cam Thanh Nipa Palm Forest (Da Nang), Mang Den Treehouse Village (Quang Ngai Province), and Huu Lien Community Tourism Village (Lang Son Province). Cat Cat Community Tourism Village (Lao Cai Province) Cat Cat village is three kilometers from Sa Pa on the road to Fansipan. Home to the Mong ethnic minority, the village dates back to the mid-19th century. Since then, it has grown into a community tourism site. Cat Cat attracts visitors who are keen to explore the culture of Vietnam's northwestern highlands. A stone path winds down the mountainside past terraced rice fields and wooden houses. Streams, water wheels, wooden bridges, and Tien Sa Waterfall form the landscape. The Mong people grow rice and practice traditional crafts like linen weaving and silver carving. Photo courtesy of Cat Cat Village Visitors can take part in festivals, learn about Mong customs, sample specialties like corn wine and thang co stew, made from the meat and offal of horses or buffaloes, and check out handicrafts. Photo courtesy of Facebook/Ban Cat Cat Huu Lien Community Tourism Village (Lang Son Province) Huu Lien sits within the Huu Lien Nature Reserve in the core zone of the Lang Son UNESCO Global Geopark. It is known for its biodiversity, with protected forests, caves, limestone mountains, and waterfalls. The village has 40 homestays and guesthouses, built in the style of stilt houses but offering most modern comforts. Photo courtesy of Lang Son Newspaper Visitors to Huu Lien can kayak on Nong Dung Lake or camp at the Michi Camp ecological site. A highlight is Dong Lam Grassland, whose look shifts with the seasons. During the rainy season, from July to October, the plain floods over and looks both dramatic and dreamlike. Photo by Hung Vi Bay Mau Cam Thanh Nipa Palm Forest (Da Nang) The Bay Mau nipa palm forest lies three kilometers from Hoi An ancient town and is bordered by the De Vong, Thu Bon, and Hoai rivers. Its brackish waters make it ideal for water coconut palms to grow. During wartime, the forest served as a revolutionary base. Today, it has become an ecotourism destination. Photo by VnExpress/Giang Huy Visitors come to Cam Thanh for basket-boat rides, an activity started in 2009 that grew popular after 2012, with basket-boat spinning performances being a main highlight. In some areas, boatmen demonstrate their spinning technique upon request, something that foreign tourists lap up. Photo by VnExpress/Giang Huy Mang Den Treehouse (Quang Ngai Province) Located near Dak Ke Lake in Mang Den Commune, the Mang Den Treehouse site was recognized as a tourist destination in August 2025. Visitors are encouraged to spend their time meditating, reading, or listening to the sounds of the forest. Photo courtesy of Mang Den Treehouse Its houses, built on tree trunks or wooden stilts amid the forest, give the site its sense of closeness to nature while respecting the ecosystem. Each features a balcony overlooking the valley or mountains. Photo courtesy of Mang Den Treehouse The place offers activities such as ziplining, cycling, and meditation, ideal for visitors seeking a retreat but with scenery to explore. Photo courtesy of Mang Den Treehouse Lo Village (Dak Lak Province) Lo Village, in Hoa Hiep Ward, spans more than 182 hectares and is home to around 10,600 people. Its name comes from the kilns once used to smoke and dry seafood, a trade that flourished decades ago. The village now has 1,500 households along the province's southern coastline, divided into three areas, with Lo 3 chosen as the site for the nomination. Lo is notable for its tiled-roof houses set among coconut trees leading straight to the sea, fishing trade, and festivals. Tourism began before 2021 as visitors sought out the fishing village's atmosphere and scenery. The village now has 72 accommodation facilities with 459 rooms. The annual Best Tourism Villages award recognizes places that balance tourism with cultural preservation, environmental protection, community support, and sustainability. Vietnam has previously won the award five times through Lo Lo Chai Village (Tuyen Quang Province), Quynh Son Cultural Village (Lang Son Province), Thai Hai Ethnic Village (Thai Nguyen Province), Tan Hoa Village (Quang Tri Province), and Tra Que Vegetable Village (Da Nang City). picked.t: Teacher spends nearly 10 years teaching Khmer in Vietnam's borderlands
picked.body: On a morning in early August, after more than two months of summer training, Ca Di watered the small garden in front of her house in Phuoc Vinh Commune. Her husband was on security duty at a school, so she sat with their eldest son, a second grader, reviewing lessons before the new school year. The youngest of four siblings, Ca Di grew up in a family of teachers. Her father and older sister were both teachers, and she developed an interest in teaching from an early age. While studying Khmer Literature Pedagogy at Tra Vinh University, she often watched reports about volunteer teachers working in remote areas and told herself she would one day do the same. In 2016, after graduating, she learned that Tan Bien District in Tay Ninh Province that borders Cambodia was recruiting primary school Khmer teachers. She took a bus more than 300 kilometers to submit her application. "I just thought I’d try. If it didn’t work out, at least it would be an experience," she recalls. Three months after taking the exam, she received her assignment to Hoa Dong Primary School. Her first days in the border region felt completely foreign, apart from the familiar curved roofs of Khmer temples among the sugar palm trees. With no relatives nearby and no guesthouses in the area, she became discouraged until a kindergarten teacher who had applied in the same recruitment round offered her a place to stay temporarily. Three months later, the school arranged accommodation in the teachers’ quarters. Once she had a place to live, another unexpected challenge emerged: the local dialect. Although both communities spoke Khmer, the dialects used in her hometown Tra Vinh and Tay Ninh differed enough to make early conversations difficult. "At first they couldn’t understand me, and I couldn’t understand them either," Ca Di says with a laugh. Some parents began to question the young teacher’s ability. Undeterred, she regularly talked with local residents to learn the area’s pronunciation and vocabulary. Only three schools in the province offer Khmer language classes, limiting opportunities for teachers to exchange experiences. At Hoa Dong Primary School, classes include both Kinh and Khmer students, so Khmer lessons are scheduled at the end of the school day. After regular classes, just over 10 students stay behind to study their mother tongue. Teaching Khmer is not easy, Ca Di says. The Khmer script has 68 vowels and consonants, nearly three times as many as Vietnamese. Students need about a year and a half just to master the alphabet, followed by more time to learn how to form syllables. Becoming proficient in reading and writing usually takes about three years. "Sometimes after finishing a new lesson, the students have already forgotten the previous one, so we have to start over. Without patience it’s easy to give up," she says. Khe Thi Sieng, now in 11th grade, still remembers her first days learning her mother tongue with Ca Di. Her parents worked as hired laborers and could not help with schoolwork, leaving Sieng self-conscious as she started from zero. Ca Di used digital lesson plans, projected images and videos about Khmer culture to make the lessons easier. She also recorded difficult words in Vietnamese to help students remember them. After nearly five years of steady effort, Sieng became fluent and one of Ca Di’s top students. Around that time, Oc Xa Quan, a school security guard who lived nearby and was 13 years older than Ca Di, was still single. After colleagues introduced them, the two began getting to know each other. "He’s the youngest of nine siblings, kind, hardworking and caring, so I felt drawn to him after a few meetings," she recalls. They married after two years and now have two sons. Besides their salaries as a teacher and school security guard, the couple farms one hectare of rice and cassava that their parents gave them. The rice mainly meets their household needs, while cassava brings in about VND20 million (US$767) per harvest in good years. Dang Cong Xuan, principal of Hoa Dong Primary School, describes Ca Di as a dedicated professional who has repeatedly completed outstanding work and received a certificate of merit from the provincial People’s Committee. She has also been recognized as a local emulation fighter and excellent teacher. "Ms. Ca Di often takes the initiative to use technology in her teaching and inspires students to love their ethnic language and script," Xuan says. According to the Tay Ninh Department of Education and Training, three primary schools in Phuoc Vinh, Tan Phu and Binh Minh wards currently offer Khmer classes to a total of 266 students. The classes are taught by only three teachers. "Every child who learns to read and write Khmer helps preserve a piece of ethnic culture for the next generation," Ca Di says.

picked.t: Vietnamese scientists develop foam that lets microbes eat pollution out of wastewater
picked.body: Holding a thin white disc no bigger than a fingertip, Mai Duc Huynh of the Department of Advanced Polymer and Composite Materials at the Institute of Materials Science, part of the Vietnam Academy of Science and Technology, called it an apartment block for microorganisms. Uniform pores inside give a single cubic meter of the material about 2,500 sq.m of surface, the equivalent of two Olympic swimming pools. Huynh registered the discs, known as porous biocarriers, under patent No. 54058 with Professor Thai Hoang, Associate Professor Nguyen Vu Giang and colleagues at the institute. Dropped into a wastewater tank by the million, the slices carry microorganisms that feed on the pollutants, a method called a moving bed biofilm reactor, or MBBR. "There are many different wastewater treatment technologies in use, but MBBR is one of the most common solutions for domestic wastewater," said Huynh, who traced the research to Vietnamese companies hunting for a high-quality domestic supply. The carrier filters nothing on its own but sits at the core of the technology. A low-surface-area carrier must be loaded in greater volume to house the same microbial mass, which means a bigger tank for the same treatment load. Spheres, cylinders and wheel-shaped carriers are cheap and easy to make, but deliver half or less the surface area per cubic meter of the foam slices, known as biochips. Biochips digest organic waste far more efficiently and cost VND40-60 million (US$1,530-2,290) per cubic meter because they are imported, Huynh said. On the disc, the surface runs along the walls of thousands of internal pores rather than sitting only on the outer face. "The challenge in making this material is controlling the porosity," he said. The foam needs interconnected pores yet has to survive knocking against tank walls, and it must be light enough to move through water without floating to the top. Reaching a stable formula took roughly two years of trial and error. Polyethylene, a thermoplastic, was chosen for its mechanical strength and its tolerance of harsh conditions. Its surface is inert and water-repellent, though, so microbes struggle to grip it. The team added proprietary additives that alter the surface chemistry and open additional small pores for microorganisms to settle in. After an initial blending, the mixture is extruded through a mold, where it foams, then air-cooled and cut into slices about 1 mm thick. The team said it built the process around plastic production lines already running in Vietnam, changing only the molds and operating settings, which it expects to cut equipment spending once production scales. Nothing has been made at that scale yet, but the team estimates material costs at 25-30% of the imported product. The foam has been tested on domestic wastewater at Hung Yen Eye Hospital and several treatment plants in Hanoi, removing 90% of organic matter along with nitrogen and meeting Vietnamese discharge standards. Huynh said the material is being refined ahead of technology transfer and mass production, aiming for a product that outperforms imports. "It is not easy to persuade a business to switch materials and change its supply chain, so we keep upgrading to create features that are not yet on the market," he said. The team wants additives that let microbial colonies establish faster, starting treatment 20% sooner than standard media. Within one to two years, the team expects Vietnamese plastic factories to be turning out the discs for manufacturing sites, farms, restaurants, clinics and any treatment system built on a tight footprint. The global MBBR market was worth $2.8 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach $5.2 billion by 2034, a compound annual growth rate of 7.8%, according to the research firm Dataintelo. Asia-Pacific accounts for roughly 38.5% of that revenue, the firm said, with thin treatment infrastructure driving demand for biological systems that can be installed quickly. It reported MBBR spreading through food processing plants, textile mills and municipal treatment stations in Vietnam, Thailand and Indonesia.

picked.t: Airport near Vietnam's hill town Da Lat welcomes first international flight since reopening
picked.body: According to the airport’s management office, AirAsia Flight AK571 from Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, landed at Lien Khuong International Airport at 10:58 a.m. on Sept. 2, bringing the first international passengers back to Da Lat. At 11:40 a.m. the same day, Flight AK572 from Da Lat to Kuala Lumpur took off, marking the resumption of scheduled international air services between Da Lat and Kuala Lumpur. The restoration of international routes is expected to provide fresh momentum for Lam Dong’s tourism sector, particularly as the province steps up destination promotion, diversifies its international visitor markets and strengthens connectivity with major tourism hubs in the region. After nearly six months of closure for rehabilitation, Lien Khuong International Airport officially resumed operations at midnight on Aug. 19, welcoming back the Da Lat–Can Tho route after nearly six years of suspension. Domestic routes linking Da Lat with major cities including Ho Chi Minh City, Hanoi, Da Nang, Vinh, Hai Phong and Can Tho have also resumed. On the international network, the Da Lat–Kuala Lumpur route is expected to operate four flights a week, while the Da Lat–Singapore route is scheduled to resume this December with three flights a week. The runway and taxiway rehabilitation project at Lien Khuong, with a total investment of more than VND1.03 trillion (US$39.24 million), commenced on March 4 this year. The project focused on rehabilitating the 3,250-meter-long and 45-meter-wide 09/27 runway, along with taxiways, safety areas, drainage systems, runway and approach lighting, and other facilities supporting flight operations. The upgraded infrastructure now accommodates Code C and D aircraft, such as the B737, B757, A320, A321, A300 and ATR72, operating at their maximum allowable loads. This is an important step in enhancing the airport's operational capacity and expanding its flight network in the coming period. In the initial phase, the airport is expected to handle around 36-40 flights a day and serve approximately 6,800 passengers daily. Passenger throughput is projected to reach around 816,000 in the final four months of 2026.
